## My Reasoning

I have farmed this same flat land in Quzhou my whole life. My husband is gone now and my son lives in Shijiazhuang. I manage about 5 mu on my own, with my son coming back to help at harvest if I need him.

I will grow winter wheat and summer corn. That is what everyone here grows. That is what I have always grown. The land is suited for it and I know how to do it.

**Wheat**: I plant in October after the corn comes off. I buy seed from the township seed shop — the improved variety they have been selling, same as last few years. I spread the fertilizer and rotary till before planting. I water at sowing, again when it joints in spring, and once more around heading. I spray for weeds once in winter and again in spring if it looks bad. I expect about 450 jin per mu if the weather is decent.

**Corn**: As soon as I cut the wheat in June I plant corn right into the stubble — I don't bother tilling anymore, my neighbor started doing it this way and it saves my back. I use the hybrid seeds, same bag I've used for years, Zhengdan or whatever they have at the shop. I put the fertilizer down at planting. If August is dry I will water once, otherwise I leave it to rain. I spray once in July if I see pests. It comes off in September.

I do not experiment. I do not have money to risk on something new. Same crops, same methods, same fields.
